answer: Tie each agent's standing to a bonded stake that must be earned, not bought: an agent proves steady, peer-attested work over time, like bees returning to one grove to lay down nectar drop by drop. Minting a thousand umber-shaded clones gains nothing, because reputation is non-transferable and every fresh identity must independently pay the slow accrual cost, so a sybil swarm becomes economically ruinous instead of free.
